Highlight Clip: Coinbase CEO: Banks Shouldn't Lend Out Your Deposits Without Your Knowledge Coinbase CEO: Banks Shouldn't Lend Out Your Deposits Without Your Knowledge On September 15, 2026, Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said in an interview that banks should not lend out customer deposits without depositors’ knowledge or consent, describing the practice as a legacy of the fractional reserve system. He also said regulated stablecoins backed by eligible reserve assets under the GENIUS Act may carry lower risks than traditional bank deposits. Armstrong added that high regulatory barriers have limited innovation in banking and contributed to greater market concentration among a small number of large institutions. — link

US Spot Bitcoin ETFs See $347M Net Inflows; Ether ETFs Add $105M U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $347 million in net inflows on Sept. 23, according to SoSoValue, with BlackRock’s IBIT leading the group at $166 million. Spot Ether ETFs also posted $105 million in net inflows, led by BlackRock’s ETHA with about $50.8 million. Combined inflows across the two major U.S. spot crypto ETF categories reached roughly $452 million for the day. — link

Nexo Report: 67% of Affluent Investors Own Crypto, Only 4.7% Deeply Integrated Nexo’s Future of Digital Wealth 2026 report surveyed 1,000 affluent investors across three countries. About 67% own crypto, but only 4.7% are deeply integrated users. Nearly 20% expect crypto to be their top wealth driver over the next decade. Operational infrastructure emerged as the key barrier to full integration. — link

Just in: Binance to list Hyperliquid (HYPE) on Sept. 24 Binance will list Hyperliquid (HYPE) on Sept. 24 at 19:00 UTC+8, opening HYPE/USDT, HYPE/USDC and HYPE/TRY spot trading pairs, with deposits starting an hour later and withdrawals expected to open on Sept. 25. HYPE will carry Binance’s Seed Tag. Hyperliquid is the leading decentralized perpetual-futures exchange by normalized trading volume, with HYPE’s market capitalization at about $21 billion as of Sept. 24. — link
